But lately, the day-to-day has just felt... well, what finally scared me into actually making this appointment, picking up the phone and calling your front desk, is that I’ve been having these really unsettling thoughts. I’ll be lying in bed, maybe the alarm is about to go off, or it's late at night, and I just think to myself, "If I didn’t wake up tomorrow, that might just be easier."

But just having that thought pop into my head out of nowhere, that maybe just not being here would be a relief from everything, from the daily grind of it all... it just really frightened me. Because that's not who I am. I'm usually the one holding everything together for everyone else at the store, making sure everything runs smoothly, so to have my brain go to such a dark, heavy place where I'm just wishing I wouldn't wake up... Well, no, not really. I mean, my appetite hasn't changed in any noticeable way, which is something, I suppose. I still eat my three meals a day, just like I always have. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, it's funny you should ask that, because it's been quite unpredictable, honestly. It's almost like my body can't quite decide what speed it wants to operate at. I've always been a very steady, deliberate person—you have to be when you're on your feet for an eight-hour shift, walking the floor, checking the stockroom, making sure everything is running smoothly. You find a pace and you stick to it. 

But lately, over the last few months, it's been so erratic. Some days, especially when I'm at home on my days off, I just can't seem to sit still. I'll find myself pacing back and forth across the living room carpet, from the sofa to the television and back again, just... restless. I don't even realize I'm doing it at first. And I've started picking at my cuticles, too, which is a terrible habit I haven't had since I was studying for my finals in college. I'll just sit there, picking and picking until my fingers are raw, feeling this sort of nervous, vibrating energy that doesn't really have anywhere to go. 

And then, on the complete opposite end of the spectrum, there are other days where everything just feels... heavy. Sluggish. Like I'm moving through molasses. Just last week, I was taking my lunch in the breakroom, and when it was time to go back out to the sales floor, the simple act of standing up and walking down the hallway felt strangely slow. Like my legs were made of lead. It took so much effort just to put one foot in front of the other and get back out to the registers. It wasn't that I was physically tired—like I said, I'm sleeping fine—it was just this profound, physical slowness. My assistant manager even asked me if I was feeling alright because I was walking so stiffly. So yes, it's either this nervous pacing and picking, or this awful, dragging sensation, and I never quite know which one it's going to be when I wake up.
